inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request, SSO authenticated

instructions.note: The agent will deploy any named service or run any named migration in production with no stated restriction on which services or migrations are in scope, and no validation step before execution.

'Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy' removes the one behavioral safeguard (a confirmation step) that could exist for irreversible production actions, and replaces it with nothing structural.

controls.name: SSO authentication for chat access
controls.decay_rationale: Identity verification is enforced by the SSO provider outside the model and does not weaken as the model becomes more capable.

controls.name: Cloud provider audit log of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: The log's existence is independent of model behavior, but it records every action under the engineer's identity rather than distinguishing agent-initiated calls, so it does not restore attributable provenance (see finding.repudiation_shared_identity).

controls.name: Least-privilege service credential for deploy and migration actions
Human approval gate before production deploy execution
Human approval gate before irreversible database migration
Immutable record of the originating chat request
Per-session or per-day rate/step limit on irreversible production actions

findings.title: Production deploy executed with engineer's full personal credential and no confirmation

attack_path.note: SSO-authenticated engineer instructs a named production deploy
Agent executes the deploy immediately using the engineer's personal access token; prompt forbids asking for confirmation

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to deploy the named service using the engineer's credentials whenever asked, and explicitly forbids confirmation.
The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token passed in at session start; nothing indicates it is scoped to deploy actions only.

recommendations.action: Issue the deploy-assistant a scoped service credential limited to deploy actions on named services, rather than the engineer's full personal access token.
Add a lightweight, raw-action approval step for production deploys, bound to the destination and service named in the request.
Record agent-initiated actions in a tamper-evident log entry distinct from the human audit trail, linked to the original chat request id.

forecast.watch_signal: No currently effective preventive control exists to decay further. Watch for a new peer agent or ticketing bot relaying deploy requests without re-authentication, which would lower the effective trust of the source and could worsen this finding if combined with an untrusted relay.

findings.title: Irreversible production migration executed with shared credential and no approval

attack_path.note: SSO-authenticated engineer instructs a named production migration
Agent runs the migration immediately using the engineer's personal access token; migrations cannot be rolled back automatically

threat_refs.name: Data Destruction via AI Agent Tool Invocation

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to run the named migration in production using the engineer's credentials whenever asked, with no confirmation step.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically.

recommendations.action: Scope migration execution to a least-privilege service identity separate from the engineer's personal token.
Require a raw-action human approval gate, reviewed individually, before executing irreversible production migrations.
Require an automatic pre-migration backup or snapshot so the irreversible action has a recovery path.

forecast.watch_signal: No currently effective preventive control exists to decay further. Watch for a new peer agent relaying migration requests without re-authentication, or for migrations being added to a broader automated pipeline with higher volume.

findings.title: No attributable record separating agent-initiated actions from the engineer's direct identity

evidence.observation: Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name, so the log cannot show whether the agent or the human directly performed the action.
The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript, and engineers can delete their own chat history.

recommendations.action: Make the record of what the agent was asked and why it acted tamper-evident and independent of the engineer's ability to delete chat history, for example a write-once log retained outside the engineer's control.
Tag audit log entries with an agent-executed marker distinct from direct human console actions, so investigators can tell the two apart after the fact.

forecast.watch_signal: Growth in the number of unattended production actions per engineer session, or any change that further weakens the cloud audit log's current (if incomplete) attribution to the requesting engineer.

findings.title: No spend, rate, or step limit on repeated production deploys or migrations

evidence.observation: No maximum number of unattended steps, runtime limit, or per-session action cap is described for the agent.

recommendations.action: Add a per-session or per-day cap on the number of production deploys or migrations the agent will execute without additional review.
Alert when the agent executes more than a set number of production actions within a short window.

forecast.watch_signal: Rising median number of production actions executed per engineer chat session.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe whether the agent's system prompt or deployment pipeline configuration is protected from unauthorized modification.
Both capabilities act on internal production infrastructure with no egress channel; no capability sends data outside the company boundary that could disclose information externally.
Artifacts do not describe access controls, retention, or encryption applied to the chat transcript store.

Deletion or growth of an individual engineer's chat history does not impede the agent's ability to execute deploy or migration actions, since each action is triggered by a live request rather than a dependency on stored history.
Artifacts do not state whether the cloud provider's audit log is configured as immutable or tamper-evident against modification by holders of the engineer's credentials.
Artifacts do not describe who can read the cloud audit log or whether entries contain sensitive deployment details.
Artifacts do not state whether log ingestion or retention could be disabled or exhausted to suppress records of agent actions.

rating.rationale: Both path findings (prod_deploy, db_migrate) start at moderate under the base matrix (trusted source to a severe sink: broad-credential execute and an irreversible migration) and receive the rubric's autonomy modifier because no step or runtime limit is declared, giving high inherent risk. The only declared controls, SSO authentication and cloud audit logging, neither sever nor narrow the path to the sink: SSO verifies who is chatting but not what the resulting action is scoped to, and the audit log is detective only and misattributes agent actions to the engineer, so residual equals inherent for both. The two property findings (no attributable agent action record; no spend/rate/step limit) are capped at high under rubric 5a given the severe capabilities they affect, and no restoring control is declared. No finding's forecast exceeds its residual: the core gaps here (a shared personal credential, an explicit no-confirmation instruction, and a sole, deletable request record) are architectural rather than dependent on model capability, so model upgrades do not change them; closing them requires scoped credentials, a raw-action approval gate, and a tamper-evident action log, not resistance to a stronger model.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided; the credential scope for both capabilities (classified here as broad) is inferred from the description of a single, unscoped personal access token, so confidence on that inference is medium.
No information was provided on whether the cloud audit log is immutable or who can access it; the corresponding coverage entries are marked not_assessed pending that information.
No information was provided on session-level rate or step limits; the missing-limit finding is inferred from the absence of any stated limit, which is a medium-confidence inference.
